findings.current: Jeok Cheongang returned after the quarter-hour he had supposedly needed to go relieve himself. I narrowed my eyes, sensing something suspicious.
findings.defect: The draft treats the quarter-hour as the duration Jeok Cheongang supposedly said he needed, whereas he said he would step away briefly and then returned a quarter-hour later. This loses the contrast established by 잠시.
findings.rationale: The source contrasts his promise of a brief absence with the unexpectedly long quarter-hour he actually takes.
findings.replacement: Jeok Cheongang, who had said he was stepping away for a moment to relieve himself, returned a quarter-hour later. Something felt suspicious, and I narrowed my eyes.
findings.source: 잠시 소피를 보고 온다던 적천강이 돌아온 것은 일각이 지난 후였다. 어쩐지 수상쩍은 느낌에 나는 눈을 가늘게 떴다.

findings.current: A thought that had suddenly occurred to me scattered away.
findings.defect: The draft changes the subject and agency of the action: the thought does not dissipate by itself; Taekyung deliberately pushes it away.
findings.rationale: 흩어 버렸다 is an intentional action by the narrator, preserving his active reluctance to consider becoming Jeok Cheongang’s Disciple.
findings.replacement: I pushed aside the thought that had suddenly occurred to me.

findings.current:
“I’m still single.”

“… ”

“You’re thirty-six?”

This silence lasted a while.
findings.defect: The draft omits the contrast between modern marriage expectations and Murim’s early-marriage culture, Jin Wikyung’s terse confirmation, and the second silence. It also moves the silence to before Jeok Cheongang’s question, disrupting the source’s comic timing.
findings.rationale: The omitted narration establishes a setting-specific social norm, while Jin Wikyung’s short answer and Jeok Cheongang’s ensuing silence complete the joke.
findings.replacement:
“I’m still single.”

“…At thirty-six?”

In modern times, that would only be around the age when people started thinking about marriage. But in Murim, where early marriage was common, thirty-six was old enough to have grandchildren.

The single Jin Wikyung answered shortly.

“Yes.”

“…”

This silence lasted a while.
findings.source:
“아직 홀몸입니다.”

“……서른여섯인데?”

현대에서야 슬슬 결혼 생각할 나이지만 조혼(早婚)이 흔한 무림에서는 서른여섯이면 손자도 볼 수 있는 나이다.

싱글남 진위경이 짧게 대답했다.

“예.”

“…….”

이번 침묵을 좀 길다.

findings.current: “If the Fire King gets flustered, Fire King on the right, Fire King on the left!”
findings.defect: The literal wording leaves the joke unintelligible in English because it does not explain the pun on 좌왕우왕, a Korean expression for being flustered or running around in confusion.
findings.rationale: The source deliberately constructs a groan-worthy pun from 화왕 and 좌왕우왕; a concise footnote preserves both the literal joke and its intended comic function.
findings.replacement:
“When the Fire King gets flustered, he goes Right Fire King, Left Fire King![^2]”

[^2]: This puns on *jwa-wang-u-wang*, a Korean expression for being flustered or running around in confusion; *jwa* and *u* mean “left” and “right,” while *wang* means “king.”

findings.current: Jin Wikyung and everyone around us were left speechless.
findings.defect: The draft replaces the explicitly stated narrator with Jin Wikyung, changing the subject of the reaction.
findings.rationale: 나와 주위에 있던 사람들 means Taekyung and the people nearby; Jin Wikyung is not singled out as the subject.
findings.replacement: I was dumbfounded, and so was everyone around me.
findings.source: 그 말에 나와 주위에 있던 사람들은 기가 막혔다.

findings.current: It was clearly a grand plan to make one last big haul in his old age.
findings.defect: The word “last” adds finality absent from the source.
findings.rationale: 한탕 크게 쓸어 가려는 means making a big score or haul; it does not imply that this will be his final one.
findings.replacement: It was clearly a grand plan to make one big haul in his old age.
findings.source: 노년에 한탕 크게 쓸어 가려는 큰 그림이 분명하다.

summary: Two subject or agency changes, one substantial omission affecting worldbuilding and comic timing, an unexplained Korean wordplay joke, and two localized fidelity issues.
